answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The hollow multiplier is published, charged in forge, and lantern lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1049 identities would post 1016 proofs and burn roughly 70 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
